paper_summary: Cheneler and Kennedy compare porous Al (salt-bead replication) with Al-Si (LM6) syntactic metal foams made by vacuum-assisted infiltration of packed beds of 2-3 mm porous expanded glass particles (EGP, 0.35 g/cc). SMFs with densities 1.00-1.19 g/cc were compression tested; stiffness, crush strength (stress at 0.25 strain) and energy absorption follow power laws in density with exponents near 3. EGP addition raises stiffness by ~2-3 GPa and crush strength by ~13 MPa relative to porous Al of equal metal fraction; FE modelling supports small reinforcement by the EGP.

structure.microstructure_notes: Relative metal density ~0.31; EGP well packed and intact after infiltration; partial infiltration of inter-particle contact regions at low pressure differential leaves inter-particle voids; matrix near-eutectic Al-Si with no reaction at interface.

test.specimen_notes: 32 mm dia x 40 mm long cylinders, 0.4 mm/s crosshead; LVDT strain; stiffness averaged over 4 load/unload cycles (25-75% of yield). strength_mpa is measured flow stress at 0.02 strain (not crush strength at 0.25 strain).

evidence.quote: Simulations estimate the stiffness of the porous aluminium and SMF to be 9.3 and 11.6 GPa respectively, higher than the 6.3 and 8.7 GPa measured for samples with near-equivalent densities.
Simulated flow stresses at 0.02 strain of 29.5 and 35.5 MPa, for the idealised porous and SMF structures respectively, are again higher than those measured (19 and 33 MPa)

for a foam density of 0.83 g/cc, the relative density is approximately 0.31. If this metal fraction remains constant and the porosity is filled with EGP with a density of 0.35 g/cc, the corresponding syntactic foam density will be approximately 1.07 g/cc.

extraction_notes: Particles are porous expanded glass beads (closed surface, 80-85% internal porosity), not hollow microballoons; classed as particle_type 'other'. Process is vacuum-assisted infiltration of a packed bed (mould preheated 300 C, melt 700 C) - coded as pressure_infiltration. Most data (40+ samples, densities 1.00-1.19 g/cc) are only shown in Figs 6, 7, 11, 12 as scatter plus power-law fits (E[GPa]=5.3237 rho^2.9171; stress at 0.25 strain [MPa]=21.814 rho^3.0858; W to 0.25 strain [MJ/m3]=4.8839 rho^2.7979), so individual values were not extracted. The single primary record uses the text-stated measured values (8.7 GPa, 33 MPa at 0.02 strain) for the SMF of 'near-equivalent density' to the 0.83 g/cc porous Al; the pairing with 1.07 g/cc and particle fraction 0.69 (=1-0.31 metal fraction) is inferred from the worked example on p.8. Strain rate 0.01/s computed from 0.4 mm/s over 40 mm specimen length. Porous Al (salt replication) results are omitted as not hollow-particle composites. Literature comparison ranges (2-4 and 5-6 MJ/m3, 1-4 GPa) omitted as ranges without specific compositions.
